Trees draw carbon dioxide out of the atmosphere and store it in their leaves, stems, branches and roots, locking it away for centuries.

The only way a forest is a permanent carbon sink is if the biomass is removed in a controlled manner and stabilized into products like 2x4s. Also worth noting, forest grow most rapidly and sequester the most carbon when they're in the earlier portion of their growth curves. Re-planting a forest after a harvest and implementing silvicultural practices such as pre-commercial thinning that optimize volume growth per acre per year until the next harvest rotation is the only way forests can act as a carbon sink.
